title: Run of the register transfer loop
statement: Let $x$ be a bit string, $B\in\mathbb{N}$, $b\in\{0,1\}$, and let $st=(K,S,P,T,Z,C,V)$ be a seven-register state. If every register is at most $B$ and $S+T\leq B$, the machine has a guarded run from label $mv(b,0)$ with state $st$ to label $incS$ when $b$ is true and $incK$ when $b$ is false, with state $(K,S+T,P,0,Z,C,V)$.
hypotheses_covered: all seven registers are at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $b$ a Boolean value, and $st$ a state
with seven natural-number registers. Suppose each register of $st$ is at most $B$ and
the sum of its registers $S$ and $T$ is at most $B$. Then, from the initial
configuration with input $x$, register values given by $st$, and control label at phase
zero of the transfer loop with parameter $b$, the machine has a run that stays within
the guard requiring the register preconditions and all register values to be at most
$B$, and reaches the configuration with control label “increment $S$” if $b$ is true and
“increment $K$” otherwise, with $T=0$ and $S$ replaced by the sum of its previous values
of $S$ and $T$, all other registers unchanged.
